page.framework: server-rendered MPA with service worker and third-party ad/consent scripts

paths.description: Campaign landing page reached from the bare URL; represents the first-visit promotional gateway.
Main news homepage; represents navigation, live scores, news discovery, consent and notification onboarding.
World Cup section listing; represents a topical listing template.
Current article; represents the primary reading template and crawler-visible editorial content.
Upcoming match detail; represents structured scores and match information.

findings.summary: No user-preference dark theme
findings.evidence: Under emulated prefers-color-scheme: dark, the root color-scheme remained normal and body stayed rgb(232,232,232) with black text; the dark screenshot retained the light page theme.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and define preference-driven surface/text tokens with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: On-load overlays are not represented by native page primitives
findings.evidence: The DOM probe found zero dialog or popover elements while the screenshot shows a notification panel and a modal consent surface layered over the page.
findings.suggestedFix: Use dialog for modal flows and popover for transient UI, with declarative dismissal and focus management.

findings.summary: Two first-visit interruptions obscure the primary content
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a notification prompt stacked with a consent modal before the news can be read or navigated.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not request notifications on arrival. Present a compact, dismissible privacy choice without stacking overlays over the core content.

findings.summary: Advertising and auxiliary chrome overwhelm editorial content
findings.evidence: The homepage screenshot is dominated by consent UI, ad slots, sponsor units, scores and side modules; the article is 11,400px tall with repeated empty/ad placeholders around a short story.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce ad density, collapse empty slots, and defer nonessential side modules until after the primary article/list content.

findings.summary: Components rely on viewport layout rather than container adaptation
findings.evidence: The stylesheet probe found no @container rule even though card and score components are reused across narrow columns and full-width regions.
findings.suggestedFix: Introduce container-type on reusable regions and size-aware @container rules for cards and score modules.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and target sizing are inadequate
findings.evidence: The focused search link computed outline:none and box-shadow:none. Of 204 visible interactive elements, 151 measured below 44px in at least one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and enlarge or pad primary touch targets to at least 44x44 CSS px.

findings.summary: First-visit overlays obstruct the reading journey
findings.evidence: Across homepage, section, article and match captures, consent and notification surfaces cover the primary navigation/content before the core reading flow can proceed.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay optional prompts, avoid stacking them, and keep reading/navigation available while privacy choices are made.

findings.summary: Unknown routes return an empty success response
findings.evidence: The unknown-route probe rendered an empty body with no title, heading, explanation, navigation or retry action; the HTTP request returned 200 with zero bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 status and a useful Arabic not-found page with home, search and retry/navigation options.

findings.summary: Core load metrics are far outside good ranges
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured homepage LCP 17.0s, TBT 1,750ms and CLS 0.304; article LCP was 18.3s and TBT 1,920ms.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP asset, defer ads/third parties, remove long tasks and reserve space for late content.

findings.summary: Late content causes severe layout movement
findings.evidence: The mobile layout observer recorded CLS 0.559 on the homepage and 0.187 on the article, with major shifts beginning around 2.6-4.1s. 89 of 91 images lacked dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve dimensions/aspect-ratio for media and ad slots and use stable font fallbacks before injecting late modules.

findings.summary: Third-party and page scripts block the main thread
findings.evidence: The trace recorded four long tasks, a longest task of 708ms and 974ms total blocking time; Lighthouse measured 1,750-1,920ms TBT.
findings.suggestedFix: Break up owned tasks and defer, conditionally load or remove ad/analytics scripts until idle or user intent.

findings.summary: Critical delivery is heavy and poorly prioritized
findings.evidence: HAR captured 173 requests and 5.18MB transferred, including parser-blocking CSS and a 1.08MB video request; LCP request discovery and dependency-tree audits failed.
findings.suggestedFix: Preload only the LCP resource, inline/split critical CSS, defer media and noncritical scripts, and apply useful cache headers.

findings.summary: Script and third-party code dominate the page load
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 60 script requests transferring 2.91MB; 136 of 173 requests and 4.18MB were third-party.
findings.suggestedFix: Audit coverage, remove duplicate/unused bundles and load ad, player and analytics dependencies only when their feature is used.

findings.summary: Controls, links, frames and images lack accessible names
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed aria-command-name/link-name/frame-title/image-alt checks; the image audit found 69 of 91 images without alt and the probe found 28 empty links.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every actionable element and iframe a meaningful name/title and meaningful images concise alt text; use empty alt only for decoration.

findings.summary: Text color contrast fails WCAG checks
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed the color-contrast audit on both homepage and article, despite controls remaining visible in the forced-colors screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust foreground/background tokens to meet WCAG AA and verify in normal, dark and forced-colors modes.

findings.summary: Heading structure and focus treatment are broken
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order and accessibility-tree audits; the homepage uses many H6 headings before content H1s injected by consent UI, and the focused search control has no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Rebuild a sequential page heading hierarchy, add a main landmark, and preserve a visible logical focus order.

findings.summary: Dense narrow columns and long empty runs impair reading
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshot compresses news into narrow multi-column modules; the mobile article extends to 11,400px with repeated empty placeholders between small text blocks.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize a readable article column, increase text/line spacing and remove empty modules that interrupt continuity.

findings.summary: The viewport disables effective user zoom
findings.evidence: Both templates set maximum-scale=1 and Lighthouse failed meta-viewport; 151 visible controls also measured below 44px.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and allow pinch zoom; enlarge primary targets and retest at 200-400% zoom.

findings.summary: Asset markup has widespread sizing and aspect-ratio problems
findings.evidence: The image audit found 89/91 images without dimensions; Lighthouse reported incorrect aspect ratio and low-resolution image failures.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide width/height or aspect-ratio, correct intrinsic ratios and responsive sources for editorial images.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs and browser lifecycle blockers remain
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported two deprecated API warnings, DevTools inspector issues, and BFCache prevention on both audited templates.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated API usage, resolve DevTools issues, and eliminate unload/lifecycle patterns that block BFCache.

findings.summary: Some navigation links are unnamed or non-crawlable
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors on homepage and article, and the probe found 28 visible empty links including href="#" controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use buttons for actions and descriptive real href anchors for navigation; provide names for image/icon links.

findings.summary: Indexing signals are inconsistent on public routes
findings.evidence: The home probe found no canonical URL; /sitemap.xml returned 404 even though robots points to a nonstandard sitemap index; an unknown route returns HTTP 200 with an empty body.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a self-referential canonical to the homepage, keep sitemap discovery consistent, and return correct 404 statuses.

findings.summary: Transport defenses and cookie attributes are unsafe
findings.evidence: The page is HTTPS but Lighthouse found one insecure request; CSP, HSTS and nosniff are absent, and all five first-party cookies observed lacked Secure and used SameSite=None.
findings.suggestedFix: Eliminate HTTP resources, set Secure and appropriate SameSite cookie attributes, then deploy CSP, HSTS and nosniff.

findings.summary: The default third-party tracking footprint is excessive
findings.evidence: Tracker capture saw 51 third-party origins and seven known trackers; HAR attributed 136 requests and 4.18MB to third parties before an affirmative privacy choice.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, gate optional analytics/ads on consent and user value, and batch essential measurement.

findings.summary: Notification solicitation appears before user intent
findings.evidence: The first viewport shows a notification prompt immediately on arrival, stacked above consent, before any notification-related user action.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask for notifications only after an explicit in-context action and explain the value immediately before the browser prompt.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: Header evidence found no clickjacking defense, Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy, in addition to missing CSP and HSTS.
findings.suggestedFix: Set CSP frame-ancestors (or X-Frame-Options), strict Referrer-Policy and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: Stacked third-party overlays create a fragile initial state
findings.evidence: Mobile captures show notification and consent surfaces stacked over content, with controls and page context competing in a 360px viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Sequence onboarding surfaces, use one top-layer primitive at a time and preserve focus/context when it closes.

findings.summary: The app-like site is not installable
findings.evidence: The page controls a service worker (netmera_sw1.js) and advertises mobile-app capability, but exposes no web app manifest.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a complete web app manifest and an intentional offline fallback, then verify installability and flaky-network behavior.

findings.summary: Failure routes degrade to a blank screen
findings.evidence: A nonexistent URL produced HTTP 200 with zero bytes and rendered no title, message, content or recovery link.
findings.suggestedFix: Return correct errors and render useful error/offline/timeout states with retry and navigation actions.

findings.summary: Arabic pages omit explicit directionality
findings.evidence: The document language is ar but html has no dir attribute; RTL relies on styling rather than an explicit semantic direction contract.
findings.suggestedFix: Set dir="rtl" on Arabic documents and migrate reusable layout spacing/alignment to logical properties.

findings.summary: Match times do not state their time-zone context
findings.evidence: The match/home view displays an upcoming kickoff as 22:00 without a visible zone or locale context, making the instant ambiguous outside the primary region.
findings.suggestedFix: Render event times with an explicit local-zone label or user-zone conversion using Intl.DateTimeFormat.

findings.summary: Consent choice architecture favors acceptance
findings.evidence: The first-layer consent modal gives a prominent Consent action and Manage options but no equivalent one-click reject action, while stating that 215 partners may use precise geolocation data.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent accept and reject choices, minimize partners/purposes and preserve easy withdrawal.

findings.summary: Images are not delivered efficiently
findings.evidence: Of 91 images, 48 use legacy formats, 40 lack srcset, 77 below-fold images are not lazy-loaded and six are oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, responsive srcset/sizes, dimensions and below-fold lazy loading.

findings.summary: Background advertising and analytics work is excessive
findings.evidence: HAR captured 36 fetch/XHR requests, 60 scripts and six media requests during an idle load; the trace still recorded long tasks after 5.5s.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not fetch media or initialize vendors until visible/user-requested; batch analytics and schedule nonessential work at background priority.

findings.summary: Third-party media cost is disproportionate to the reading task
findings.evidence: The page transferred 5.18MB, including 4.18MB third-party bytes and a 1.08MB video fetched without the user requesting video.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove autoplay/background media, gate players on interaction and enforce per-template third-party and media budgets.

findings.summary: The idle homepage has a very large memory/DOM footprint
findings.evidence: The baseline heap summary contained 1,147,497 nodes and 64.0MB self size before a reading interaction, disproportionate for a news homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce ad/player SDKs and hidden DOM, virtualize long repeated modules, and track heap/DOM budgets in regression tests.

taskList.title: Remove stacked first-load prompts and make consent choices symmetric
Cut third-party scripts, trackers and automatic video loading
Repair LCP, layout stability and resource priority
Restore names, heading order, visible focus, zoom and target sizes
Deploy transport headers and secure cookie policy
Optimize responsive image delivery and reserve dimensions
Return a real, useful 404 and resilient network states
Reduce ad chrome and restore a readable article flow
Add dark-mode tokens and RTL/time-zone semantics
Reduce hidden DOM and enforce memory budgets
